summary: Backend-only testing of the new force_degraded health simulator. All 10 pytest cases pass against the live preview URL. Query-param single-shot behavior, admin flip/state/clear flow, non-admin rejection (403), 3600s cap, and regression on 4 admin endpoints all verified. State cleared after run; self-ping loop confirmed still emitting healthy 200 heartbeats.
critical_code_review_comments: _FORCE_DEGRADED_UNTIL_TS uses time.monotonic() which is process-local — in a multi-worker/uvicorn setup with >1 worker, the admin flip would only affect the worker that handled the POST; other workers would still report ok. Not currently an issue on this pod (single worker) but worth noting if scaled out.

Admin POST body is required (Pydantic model). Sending an empty body returns 422 rather than defaulting to duration_sec=900. Minor UX / doc note — the code comment says default 15 min but you can't hit it via an empty POST.
Ideal: add a test that asserts self-ping alerting path (mock httpx to feed 2 consecutive degraded); currently out of scope but would round out coverage.
seed_data_creation: None. Every test both pre- and post-clears the global force-degraded timer via the admin endpoint (autouse fixture) so the pod is left in a clean status=ok state — no risk of a real Slack alert firing after the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file /app/backend/tests/test_force_degraded.py is a reusable regression for the force-degraded pipeline. 10 cases, 7.5s runtime, uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. If retesting, note the autouse cleanup fixture clears the timer before AND after every test so ordering does not matter. Baseline /api/health returned {status:ok, uptime>0, db.ok:true, mailer.breaker_open:false} and self-ping logs show `[self-ping] Heartbeat ping status: 200` every ~5 min.
